editorial:
Imagine feeling like a stranger in your own hometown. That is exactly where you find Jimmie, a guy who just wants to get back the beautiful house his grandfather built decades ago. He is not alone, though, because his funny and loyal best friend Mont is right there by his side. Together, they wander through a version of San Francisco that feels like a dream, looking at a city that has become way too expensive for people like them. The whole vibe is very calm and pretty, making you feel the deep bond between the two friends as they try to find where they truly fit in.

You will love how the acting feels real and not forced. The chemistry between the leads is the best part, though the story moves quite slowly, which might bore some of you. If you appreciate beautiful shots of the city and a heartfelt story about family, you should definitely give this a try. For the best experience, I suggest streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see every detail of the architecture, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: After breaking into the house and spending a night there, Jimmie finally realizes that the building is just a shell. He learns that holding onto the past cannot bring back his family or change the city. He decides to let the house go and stop fighting a losing battle. He walks away from the property, choosing his friendship with Mont and his own peace of mind over a piece of real estate.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about friendship, family roots, and beautiful scenery.
